title: Subtract Second Half From First
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list of length `n`, modify the first `floor(n / 2)` nodes in-place so that for each 0-based index `0 <= i < floor(n / 2)`, the `i`-th node's value becomes `node[i].val - node[n - 1 - i].val`, where `node[n - 1 - i]` is its mirror node in the second half.

Leave the middle node (when `n` is odd) and all nodes in the second half unchanged, and return the head of the modified list. Solve in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: Use fast and slow pointers (`while fast.next and fast.next.next`) so `slow` stops at the last node before the strict second half (`slow.next` has length `floor(n / 2)`).
Reverse `slow.next`, walk the first half and reversed second half in lockstep to subtract values, then reverse the second half back and re-attach it to `slow.next`.

examples.explanation: Pairs (10, 40) and (20, 30) update the first two nodes to 10-40=-30 and 20-30=-10, keeping [30, 40].
First 2 nodes subtract mirror nodes [5, 4] giving [1-5, 2-4] = [-4, -2]; middle 3 and second half [4, 5] stay unchanged.
With 1 node, floor(1/2) = 0 nodes change, so [7] stays [7].
